direct_evidence: Transaction includes dealer code, item, engine number, chassis number, brand, color and end-customer identity.
Sales Tax 18% and N.E.V Levy are separate visible financial fields.
inferences: Likely corresponds to the Dealer Customer Invoice menu entry, but the exact launch path is not directly shown.
unknowns: Meaning of Company Name versus Brand.
Whether Cost Price is editable, derived, or lookup-based.

accounting_evidence: Outgoing payment voucher supports multiple accounting lines.
Voucher can carry Ref Inv and Booking # references.
Total field is shown below the detail grid.

images.screen_type: bike advance booking / customer reservation form
direct_evidence: Booking captures desired item and color.
Booking captures amount, advance and balance.
Booking includes delivery date and status.
workflow_evidence: WAITING is an observed booking status.
The screenshot proves a reservation/advance record exists before or independently of a fully identified engine/chassis sale.
inferences: A specific engine/chassis may be allocated later because no engine/chassis fields are visible here.
Remaining balance may later be collected through Cash Balance Receive, but that relation is not yet proven.

cross_image_findings: Booking references appear on the Cash Payment Voucher, establishing at least a visible reference surface between booking and accounting.
Dealer Customer records engine/chassis while Advance Booking Customer records item/color; this may represent model-level reservation followed by unit allocation.
Customer identity/contact fields are embedded in both transaction-style forms.
